newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Tirtamas Group to take over Bank Niaga.
newsitem.headline: Tirtamas Group to take over Bank Niaga.

text.p: Indonesia's Tirtamas Group announced on Monday it would take over Bank Niaga, the sixth-largest private bank in Indonesia, in the largest corporate acquisition this year in the country.
Brokers estimated Tirtamas would invest about 756 billion rupiah ($293.6 million) in its plan to acquire a 50 percent stake in the bank.

Tirtamas said it would buy the 40 percent stake in the bank held by controlling shareholders, the Tahija family, at a price of 8,000 rupiah per share. It also said it would buy an additional 10 percent from the public at the same price.
Tirtamas unit PT Tunasmas Paduarta will buy the 40 percent stake from two companies held by Julius Tahija and his sons, the group said in a statement.
Bank Niaga shares soared on news of the acquisition. The share closed at 7,750 rupiah, up 1,050.

"Bank Niaga is one of the largest, most profitable and most professionally run Indonesian private banks, and we felt fortunate to be entrusted with it by the Tahija family," Tirtamas chairman Hashim Djojohadikusumo said in the statement.
"Tirtamas will continue Bank Niaga's successful business strategy and solid progress. In addition, we are committed to strengthening Bank Niaga's capital base."

Tirtamas is the controlling shareholder of cement company Semen Cibinong. It also has large stakes in various banks and financial companies including Bank Papan Sejahtera, Merrill Lynch Indonesia, Bank Kredit Asia, Bank Pelita and MetLife Sejahtera Insurance.
"Hashim is building up a banking empire," said the research head of one foreign brokerage. "He wants to establish himself as a major player and this is the first major bank he has got."
The research head said Hashim would probably take his stake in Bank Niaga up to 60 percent and allow it to absorb some operations from his smaller banks.
There was no immediate word on how Tirtamas would finance the deal, although the research head said it had been under negotiation for some time.
The Tirtamas statement also quoted Julius Tahija as saying that his family would focus on activities other than banking.

"At this stage of the development of the family portfolio of investments, we have concluded that we would rather focus our resources on our emerging activities, which include power generation, insurance, mining, plantations development and fund management," Tahija was quoted as saying.

"Based on that decision, it became easier to react positively to the approach from Tunasmas. The decision to sell was difficult; however, my family and I are pleased to see our holding pass to the hands of a strong, respected group which has the vision, financial capability and business skills to support and guide the bank in its next stage of development." ($ = 2,575 rupiah)
